draft.title: Capturing carbon
card: Carbon capture means taking carbon dioxide out of the air and holding it as carbon in another store. Forests do this when trees grow, because photosynthesis builds carbon into wood and leaves.
Soils and oceans also take up carbon naturally. Soils hold carbon in dead plant matter. Oceans absorb carbon dioxide from the air, and it dissolves in the water.

First Nations Australians have long managed fire on Country. Cool, planned burns early in the dry season can reduce large, hot fires later in the year. Hot fires release much more carbon, so this can help keep more carbon stored in plants and soil.
New technologies can help too. Some machines capture carbon dioxide from the air or from factory smoke, and it can then be stored deep underground.
draft.remember: Carbon can be captured by nature and by people, and each way holds carbon out of the air.

a.q: Why can planting a new forest reduce the carbon dioxide in the air?
opts: Growing trees take in carbon dioxide and build it into wood
Trees make carbon dioxide into water that falls as rain
Trees give out carbon dioxide that is then stored in soil
Trees block heat from reaching the air above the forest
a.why: Growing trees use photosynthesis to take carbon dioxide from the air and build it into wood and leaves, so the carbon is stored. Trees do not turn carbon dioxide into rain, and they do not release it as a way of storing it.
a.clue: Think about what trees take in as they grow.

b.q: A ranger group in northern Australia lights cool, planned burns early in the dry season. How can this help store carbon?
opts: It can reduce hot fires that release much more carbon
It removes all plants so that no carbon is released later
It adds carbon dioxide to the soil to help plants grow
It turns the carbon in the plants into rock underground
b.why: Cool, planned burns can reduce large, hot fires later in the year. Hot fires release much more carbon, so fewer of them leaves more carbon stored in plants and soil. The burns do not remove all plants or make rock.
b.clue: Compare the carbon released by cool burns and by hot fires.

a.best: Growing trees take in carbon dioxide and build it into wood

b.best: It can reduce hot fires that release much more carbon
